title: Words and surprises
purpose: The school's words as the site uses them, and why the site says what it says when it surprises you.

sections.title: Skill
paras: What a child can do, in one sentence. Each skill belongs to a topic and has levels.

sections.title: Topic
paras: A group of skills, such as addition. A topic is marked taught for one class at a time.

sections.title: Level
paras: How hard a skill's questions are. The school's levels, easiest first, are {levels}. Each level has its own sentence and rule.

sections.title: Home assessment
paras: A child's own paper, on the one skill they most need, approved by an educator. See [how it is chosen](/guide/worked-out#home-assessment).

sections.title: A check that places a child
paras: A short paper on a skill showing {colour:grey}, so the site can say where the child stands.

sections.title: Check answers
paras: Looking at an answer the engine was not sure of and saying what the child wrote.

sections.title: Sign off
paras: Saying, in your name, that the answers on a paper are settled. Only signed off answers count.

sections.title: Spot check
paras: An answer the engine was sure of, still shown to a person now and then to keep the reader honest.

sections.title: Printed code
paras: The code on every printed page. It says which paper and which child the page is, so the engine never guesses.

sections.title: Spare
paras: An extra paper with no name, for a spoilt page or a child who arrives late.

sections.title: {colour:green}, {colour:amber}, {colour:red}, {colour:grey}
paras: The four colours a skill can show. Each has a word and a mark, never colour alone. See [what each colour means](/guide/worked-out#states).

sections.title: Why was an answer left for a person to check?
paras: Every wrong answer and every blank is checked by a person before it counts.
A right answer is checked too until the reader is trusted on that kind of question, and some are spot checked after.
The card on Check answers says the reason in one sentence. The rules are on [How it is worked out](/guide/worked-out#trust).

sections.title: Why does a skill show {colour:grey} when the child did the paper?
paras: Only signed off answers count. Answers still waiting for a person do not count yet.
Blanks are left out of the count. A skill needs at least {t:state.min_events} answers that are right or wrong.
Answers on a paper that was replaced do not count.

sections.title: Why is a skill {state:practising} when most answers were right?
paras: A skill is {state:secure} only when it is seen on at least {t:state.min_observers} papers, with {t:next_sheet.promote_at|pct} or more right.
A mistake made more than once shows as {state:patterned_error}, whatever the share right.

sections.title: Why does a child's grade differ from the class's?
paras: A child has their own grade on the class list. A class shows the grade most of its children are in.
A child's papers are drawn from their own grade's levels, so a child in another grade from the class gets their own grade's work.

sections.title: Why did a wrong answer count against another skill?
paras: A wrong answer with a known mistake counts against the skill that mistake belongs to, which may not be the question's own skill.
A right answer counts for every skill the question used.
